theory.intro: To subtract a fraction from a whole number, rename one whole as a fraction with the same denominator, then subtract.
facts: One whole can be renamed using equal parts: $1=\frac{3}{3}=\frac{5}{5}$.
To find the part missing from one whole, subtract the part you know. Keep the parts the same size.
For a whole bigger than $1$, keep the extra wholes and only rename one of them.
steps: Rename one whole using the same denominator as the fraction.
Combine with any remaining wholes and simplify.

workedExamples.question_text:
A strip has $\frac{5}{8}$ shaded.
(a) What fraction is unshaded? Check that the two parts make one whole.
(b) Why must one whole be renamed as eighths before subtracting?
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) One whole is $\frac{8}{8}$.
$1-\frac{5}{8}=\frac{8}{8}-\frac{5}{8}=\frac{3}{8}$
The unshaded part is $\frac{3}{8}$.
$\frac{5}{8}+\frac{3}{8}=\frac{8}{8}=1$
(b) The parts must be the same size. Renaming $1$ as $\frac{8}{8}$ lets us subtract the number of eighths while keeping the denominator $8$.

workedExamples.question_text:
Calculate $6-\frac{7}{10}$.
Explain why the answer is greater than $5$.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Keep $5$ wholes and rename the remaining whole as $\frac{10}{10}$.
$6-\frac{7}{10}=5+\frac{10}{10}-\frac{7}{10}=5\frac{3}{10}$
Only part of the sixth whole was removed, so there are still $5$ wholes and $\frac{3}{10}$.

The $12$ complete wholes cancel, leaving one whole minus $\frac{2}{3}$.
$13-12\frac{2}{3}=1-\frac{2}{3}=\frac{3}{3}-\frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$
It is $\frac{1}{3}$ less than $13$.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) Find the missing numerator: $1-\frac{\square}{11}=\frac{4}{11}$.
(b) Check that the removed and remaining parts make one whole.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) One whole has $11$ elevenths. If $4$ elevenths remain, $11-4=7$ elevenths were removed.
The missing numerator is $7$.
(b) $\frac{7}{11}+\frac{4}{11}=\frac{11}{11}=1$

foundation.question_text: Find the complement of $\frac{3}{8}$ to one whole.

A whole strip has $\frac{4}{9}$ shaded.
What fraction is unshaded?

development.solution_text:
One whole has $12$ twelfths. If $5$ twelfths remain, $12-5=7$ twelfths were removed.
$x=7$

development.question_text:
A tank is $\frac{7}{10}$ full.
What fraction of its capacity is empty?

A student writes $1-\frac{3}{7}=\frac{1-3}{7}$.
Explain the error and correct it.
development.solution_text:
One whole must be renamed as $\frac{7}{7}$.
$1-\frac{3}{7}=\frac{7}{7}-\frac{3}{7}=\frac{4}{7}$

mastery.question_text: Calculate $2-\frac{15}{16}$ and explain why the answer is greater than $1$.
mastery.solution_text:
$2-\frac{15}{16}$
$=1+\frac{16}{16}-\frac{15}{16}$
$=1\frac{1}{16}$
Only part of one of the two wholes was removed.
